{
  "need": "Status",
  "secondary": { "name": "Competence" },
  "read": "This student needs to know you see them as capable of genuine growth, not as a suspect. If you come in accusatory, you signal that the only believable story about them is a low one, which is a direct hit to their sense of mattering. The competence angle is real too: if this actually is a breakthrough, they may not yet trust that they can replicate it, so the conversation needs to protect that fragile new confidence rather than crush it.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Enforcer", "instinct": "Demanding they explain themselves or citing the gap in quality as evidence of wrongdoing, which turns a possible win into an interrogation and tells them you assume the worst about who they are." },
  "mentorMove": "Lead with genuine curiosity and treat the strong work as real until evidence says otherwise. Your job is to invite them to walk you through their thinking, not to catch them, and to hold the standard that you need to see their process, not as punishment but as a normal part of how serious writers and thinkers work.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "You need to see evidence of their thinking, not just the finished product.",
    "The standard is that work submitted under their name reflects their own understanding."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "How they show you their process can vary: a conversation, a follow-up draft, walking through their choices out loud.",
    "If they used outside resources legitimately, that is fine to acknowledge; the question is whether they can own the ideas."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 2, "label": "Questions" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey, I read your piece last night and honestly it stopped me. I want to talk about it with you for a couple of minutes." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "Walk me through how you got here. What was going on in your head when you wrote this section? Where did this idea come from?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I need from you, and I ask this of anyone whose work makes a real leap: help me see the thinking behind it. That might be talking it through with me right now, or showing me an earlier draft or some notes. It is how we make sure the growth is yours to build on." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "I hold everyone to the standard that what you put your name on, you can stand behind and explain. I am holding you to that same bar because this work is strong and I genuinely believe you are the person who can meet it. So let us figure out together how you show me that." }
  ],
  "longGame": "If the work is authentic, this conversation becomes a milestone: the moment an adult took their growth seriously enough to dig into it rather than ignore it or doubt it. If something else is going on, a low-pressure process conversation surfaces it early, before it becomes a bigger integrity issue, and keeps the relationship intact for what comes next."
}
situation: A student handed in work far better than anything they have produced before, and I genuinely cannot tell if it is a breakthrough or if someone else did it.
